accepted.s: Which one of the following best explains the role of small industries in the Indian economy?
o: They mainly reduce agricultural employment without affecting regional development
They are labour-intensive, require relatively little capital and help disperse industries to rural and semi-urban areas
They depend exclusively on imported technology and raw materials
They are capital-intensive and promote industrial concentration in metropolitan areas
accepted.x: Small industries are labour-intensive, require little capital and help disperse industrial activity to rural and semi-urban areas.
accepted.tq: Identify the option combining the core employment, capital and dispersal functions.
accepted.sec: Role of small and cottage industries - employment, dispersal, concentration of economic power, small-scale policies

accepted.s: Small industries help reduce concentration of economic power primarily because they—
o: operate only under direct government ownership
spread industrial ownership and economic activity across wider regions and groups
accepted.x: Small industries disperse ownership of wealth and economic activity, thereby reducing the concentration of economic power.
accepted.tq: Apply the economic meaning of dispersal of ownership to the situation described.
accepted.sec: Role of small and cottage industries - employment, dispersal, concentration of economic power, small-scale policies

accepted.s: Small-scale industries have been treated as a priority in India since which Plan?
accepted.x: Small-scale industries have been a policy priority since the First Five-Year Plan.
accepted.tq: Use direct plan-period recall for a policy-origin question.
accepted.sec: Role of small and cottage industries - employment, dispersal, concentration of economic power, small-scale policies

accepted.s:
The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1948 identified which of the following as handicaps of small industries?
1. Shortage of raw materials
2. Inadequate finance
3. Marketing difficulties
4. Lack of technology
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The IPR 1948 identified difficulties relating to raw materials, finance, marketing and technology. All four statements are correct.
accepted.tq: Recognise the complete list of handicaps rather than selecting only familiar items.
accepted.sec: Role of small and cottage industries - employment, dispersal, concentration of economic power, small-scale policies

accepted.s: The Karve Committee was primarily associated with which of the following objectives?
o: Providing only export subsidies to large industries
Deregulating foreign trade and abolishing all small industries
Avoiding technological unemployment, maximising employment in the Second Plan and promoting decentralised development
accepted.x: The Karve Committee proposed avoiding technological unemployment, maximising employment during the Second Plan and promoting decentralised development.
accepted.tq: Match the committee with its distinctive policy objectives.

accepted.s: The Karve Committee relating to village and small industries was constituted in—

accepted.s:

accepted.s:
Arrange the following committees in chronological order of their association with the small-scale or MSME sector:
A. Abid Hussain Committee
B. Karve Committee
C. U.K. Sinha Committee
D. S.P. Gupta Committee
E. P.R. Nayak Committee
Select the correct answer.
accepted.x: The correct sequence is Karve (1955), Nayak (1992), Abid Hussain (1997), S.P. Gupta (2001) and U.K. Sinha (2019).
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest committees first, then place the intervening years.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the contribution and linkages of MSMEs?
o: MSMEs reduce the spread of ownership of wealth.
MSMEs function as ancillaries to large industry and help reduce regional imbalances.
MSMEs are legally prohibited from supplying large industries.
MSMEs increase regional concentration by restricting activity to metropolitan areas.
accepted.x: MSMEs act as ancillary units to large industries, reduce regional imbalances and spread ownership of wealth more evenly.
accepted.tq: Select the option containing the complete positive linkage of MSMEs with the wider economy.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Emergency Credit Line Guarantee Scheme (ECLGS)?
o: It was launched in 2017 only for delayed-payment disputes.
It was introduced in 1951 exclusively for state financial corporations.
It is an RBI platform for discounting receivables.
It was a Covid-era emergency credit scheme introduced in 2020.
accepted.x: ECLGS was a Covid-era emergency credit scheme associated with 2020.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the scheme’s crisis context and year from those of other credit instruments.

accepted.s: Which statement correctly distinguishes the two loan limits stated for MSE lending in February 2026?
o: No collateral is required up to ₹25 lakh, while banks may lend only up to ₹20 lakh.
No collateral is required up to ₹20 lakh, while banks may extend the limit up to ₹25 lakh.
